title: Steak sandwich or sub on wheat

content.title: About
content.content: A steak sandwich or sub on wheat is a layered sandwich that features thinly sliced, cooked steak placed between halves of a whole‑grain wheat roll. It is often topped with vegetables, cheese, sauces, and spices, making it a hearty and flavorful meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A wheat roll provides slower‑releasing carbohydrates compared with a white roll.
The steak is usually grilled or pan‑seared with seasonings to enhance its aroma.
Steak subs are a staple of American fast‑casual cuisine, especially in sandwich chains.
The combination of protein and complex carbs makes this sandwich a good source of sustained energy.
Variations may include caramelized onions, jalapeños, or barbecue sauce.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beef is an excellent source of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed and supports healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: The whole‑grain wheat roll delivers slow‑release glucose, helping maintain stable blood sugar.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat adds fiber, which aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Beef can contain saturated fats, so individuals with high cholesterol should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and processed toppings may increase salt levels, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat roll contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of meat, cheese, and sauces, the sandwich can be calorie‑rich; portion control is advised for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich fresh, cutting it in half if desired. Add fresh veggies such as tomato, lettuce, or cucumber, and choose mustard, mayo, or barbecue sauce to taste. For extra crunch, lightly toast the roll before assembling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped in plastic film or placed in an airtight container. Keep the wheat roll in a dry place, and store cooked steak separately at ≤4 °C.
